titulo: Quiz — O-kaikei — the number you see is already the whole number
subtitulo: Tax inside the price, the register by the door, no tip to work out
introPt: A traveller closes a meal: asks for the bill, hears the total, names the method and carries the slip to the register.
cenario: The end of dinner at a full counter.

dialogo.es: お会計をお願いします。
dialogo.tts: お会計をお願いします。

dialogo.es: かしこまりました。お会計はあちらのレジでお願いします。
dialogo.pt: Certainly. Please pay at the register over there.
dialogo.tts: かしこまりました。お会計はあちらのレジでお願いします。

dialogo.es: カードでお願いします。
dialogo.tts: カードでお願いします。

dialogo.es: 申し訳ありません、当店は現金のみです。
dialogo.tts: 申し訳ありません、当店は現金のみです。

perguntas.pergunta: What does the price shown on the menu mean for you?
opcoes: Tax will be added at the register
The tax is already inside the displayed price, so it is normally the figure you pay
You must add a tip on top
It applies only at the counter
perguntas.explica: Total-price display is required by law; a サービス料, where a place has one, is posted in advance.

perguntas.pergunta: In most restaurants and cafés, where do you settle the bill?
opcoes: At the table, by waving for a pen
At the register on the way out, carrying the 伝票 slip
Online afterwards
You do not — service is prepaid
perguntas.explica: The slip is left on your table; you carry it to the レジ at the front and pay there.

perguntas.pergunta: You need paperwork for work expenses. Which do you ask for?
opcoes: The レシート, which is enough
Nothing — the card statement counts
A 領収書, the formal receipt, asked for by name
A photo of the menu
perguntas.explica: A レシート is the ordinary till slip; a 領収書 is the formal receipt, and staff may ask what name to write.

perguntas.pergunta: A small place has a posted cash-only sign and refuses your card. Is that allowed?
opcoes: Yes — nothing obliges a business to take a card, and cash always settles the bill
No, cards must be taken for any amount
Only outside Tokyo
Only if they also take IC cards
perguntas.explica: Many small or family-run places are cash only, which is normal and lawful; keep a float of yen.

perguntas.pergunta: What percentage should you tip in Japan?
opcoes: Ten per cent
Fifteen per cent
Five per cent at lunch, ten at dinner
None — there is no tipping; coins left behind get chased after you
perguntas.explica: There is no tip. What closes a meal is gochisousama deshita on the way out.
